title: Finding the Ground: A Plane Fitted by Random Samples, Why a Least Squares Plane Is Pulled Off by What Stands on It, and a Ground That Is Not the Biggest Plane

questions.question: Why is a least squares plane fitted to every point a poor ground?
options: The things standing on the ground pull it up towards them
It cannot be computed for more than a few points
It ignores the points far from the sensor
It only works on level ground
questions.explanation: The fit minimises squared heights, so points a metre up on a box pull it hard. The more there is standing on the ground, the worse the ground comes out.

questions.question: With boxes on the ground, the least squares plane was tilted:
options: 5.00 degrees
5.08 degrees
6.57 degrees
90 degrees
questions.explanation: On the bare ground it found the 5 degree tilt to a tenth of a degree. With 450 points on boxes at the far end it tilted up to meet them.

questions.question: RANSAC found:
options: 6.57 degrees
5.00 degrees exactly
5.08 degrees
0.2 degrees
questions.explanation: The plane with the most points within 3 cm of it had 82 percent of them. The boxes' points were not near it, so they did not count.

questions.question: How many draws made a clean sample 99 percent likely at a share of 85 percent?
questions.explanation: A draw is clean when all three points are on the ground, with probability 0.85 cubed. Five draws make at least one clean with 99 percent confidence.

questions.question: Why was the wall taken for the ground?
options: The tolerance of 3 cm was too tight
The seed was unlucky
The wall was closer to the sensor
It held the most points, and nothing said the ground is level
questions.explanation: The wall had 1200 points and the ground 600. An unconstrained search returned the wall; refusing planes tilted more than 30 degrees gave the ground.

questions.question: Why can the same seed be relied on?
options: A random method gives the same answer for any seed
The draws are repeatable, so a test gives the same answer
The points are sorted first
Three points always define the same plane
questions.explanation: The generator is deterministic, so a given seed draws the same triples. That is what lets a test of a random method have one right answer.
